routes.title: Limited check of largest-cluster finite-size scaling
routes.hypothesis: At the paper's Manhattan critical probability p = 0.6971571, the ensemble mean largest SCC fraction decreases with even lattice size L, approximately as L^(1.8035-2). Compare measured size dependence with this prediction using uncertainty across independent realizations. A stable incompatible trend would challenge consistency within the tested size range; agreement would be a limited numerical check, not reproduction of the paper's precision.
routes.rationale: Accept as a bounded consistency check using a new paper-based implementation. Seed Section II defines the lattice, Section III A supplies SCC methods, and Section IV C, Eqs. (8) and (10), implies mean largest SCC fraction proportional to L^(-0.1965) at criticality, subject to finite-size corrections. Two fixed even sizes can form the two arms: each returns the running mean of max(component size)/L^2 at identical realization-count checkpoints. Their final-mean ratio can be compared with (L_large/L_small)^(-0.1965). This measures one size contrast, not a reliable asymptotic exponent. Assume periodic boundaries, even L >= 4 to avoid the L=2 nearest-neighbor ambiguity, alternating row/column orientations, direct independent Bernoulli occupation at p=0.6971571, and singleton inclusion. Python with NumPy/SciPy or a disclosed SCC implementation is sufficient in principle. No repository code exists in the supplied record to inspect; implementation correctness and runtime remain unverified. Select this baseline before interpreting orientation perturbations. Acceptance concerns feasibility, not an approved execution specification or demonstrated agreement.
risks: Small-size corrections can produce disagreement without contradicting the paper's asymptotic prediction.
Two sizes provide only one contrast; a credible exponent estimate needs more sizes and stability checks.
The metric denominator is L^2 separately in each arm; comparing raw largest-component counts would test a different prediction.
Running-mean checkpoints are correlated and cannot be treated as independent uncertainty samples.
Approved sizes, seeds, realization counts, uncertainty procedure, tolerances and compute budget are absent.
The proposed small check cannot reproduce the paper's million-realization precision or establish universality.

routes.title: Finite-size response to random orientation reversals
routes.hypothesis: At fixed p = 0.6971571 and matched finite L, independently reversing each Manhattan bond with probability 0.1 reduces the ensemble mean largest SCC fraction relative to reversal probability zero. Use paired occupation randomness and compare the difference across independent seeds. This is an agent-defined perturbation test; it does not measure a shifted critical point or establish a universality class.
routes.rationale: Accept as a feasible, agent-generated finite-size perturbation test after validating the baseline implementation. At a fixed even L >= 4 and p=0.6971571, compare reversal probabilities 0 and 0.1 using the same occupation uniforms for corresponding underlying bonds. Generate independent reversal randomness, redraw orientations for every realization, and reverse bonds before occupation while retaining exactly one possible directed bond per nearest-neighbor pair. Both arms return running means of max(component size)/L^2 on the same realization-count axis. Suppression is a falsifiable prediction, not a consequence established by the cited sources: reversals can both destroy and create directed cycles. Seed page 13 motivates alternative arrangements broadly, but the quoted passage specifically discusses resistor-diode variants and does not establish this rule. Wang–Li allows antiparallel bonds; Janus uses spatial neighbor selection with a degree constraint. Neither provides a quantitative control for this perturbation. Defer execution selection until the baseline has been validated; no critical-point shift or universality conclusion follows from this fixed-p comparison.
risks: A finite-size response at the original Manhattan critical probability does not locate the perturbed model's critical point.
Independent reversals alter local in/out-degree balance but do not necessarily introduce a preferred global direction.
Changing random-number consumption between arms can break intended occupation pairing unless streams are explicitly separated.
Uncertainty must use independent paired realizations or paired replicate endpoints, not correlated running-mean checkpoints.
The scalar output does not expose per-realization variance; uncertainty requires a supervisor-approved replicate protocol or approved checkpoints retaining recoverable samples.
Passing the baseline does not support the untested suppression hypothesis or establish scientific novelty.

limitations: The interval is exploratory, with no sequential or multiple-testing correction; the result-selected follow-up has the same limitation.
Eight independent paired endpoints determine uncertainty; correlated running means are not additional independent samples.
Shared seeds do not establish bondwise coupling between different lattice sizes.
Sanity and replay passes do not independently validate periodic orientations, edge uniqueness or SCC correctness.
No ratio uncertainty or approved quantitative scaling comparison is supplied, so compatibility with the proposed exponent remains untested.
The follow-up changes the size contrast and cannot resolve the original L=16 effect magnitude; that requires additional independent samples at the original sizes.
Source evidence and literature coverage are limited; these finite-size measurements do not establish novelty, universality, orientation-reversal suppression or real-world validity.
Runtime at L=32 remains unmeasured, and no comparable discovery-process baseline supports an acceleration multiplier.
next_decision.next_experiment: Compare L=32 with the fixed L=8 baseline to test whether the decrease persists across a wider size contrast.
next_decision.rationale: Round 1 (rounds/01) measured means of 0.5772705078125 and 0.502197265625, normalized by 64 and 256 sites respectively. The paired difference was -0.0750732421875, with exploratory 95% interval [-0.12436767431356628, -0.02577881006143372] across eight paired endpoints. This excludes zero but crosses -0.05. Sanity and replay passed, supporting empty-graph normalization and repeatability, without establishing general implementation correctness. The observed decrease shifts the next decision toward testing persistence at L=32 against the unchanged L=8 baseline. Keep 16 realizations and checkpoints 1 through 16, normalizing treatment by 1024 sites. This parameter change fits the implementation bounds and planned configuration-count budget; the supervisor must enforce runtime limits. Metric, baseline and thresholds remain unchanged.
next_decision.result_interpretation: The L=16 mean was lower than the L=8 mean, but the exploratory interval does not establish a decrease exceeding 0.05.

summary.interval_method: Paired-seed Student t interval, 95%; exploratory, no sequential or multiple-testing correction.

limitations: The interval is exploratory and lacks sequential or multiple-testing correction; L=32 was selected after observing round 1.
Eight independent paired endpoints determine uncertainty; running means at checkpoints 1 through 16 are correlated and are not additional independent samples.
Shared seeds do not establish bondwise coupling across different lattice sizes.
Sanity and replay passes do not independently validate periodic Manhattan orientations, edge uniqueness, vertex coverage or SCC correctness.
No approved ratio uncertainty analysis or quantitative scaling tolerance is supplied, so the proposed exponent remains untested.
The L=32 contrast does not resolve the magnitude of the original L=16 effect, and these small lattices may exhibit substantial finite-size corrections.
Limited source and literature coverage provides insufficient evidence for scientific novelty, universality, orientation-reversal suppression or real-world validity.
Raw artifacts and runtime measurements were not independently inspected here, and no comparable discovery-process baseline establishes an acceleration multiplier.
next_decision.next_experiment: After independent graph validation, repeat the L=8 versus L=32 comparison with fresh paired seeds and a preregistered sample count and analysis.
next_decision.rationale: Round 2 (rounds/02) reports control mean 0.577392578125 and treatment mean 0.46033477783203125, normalized by 64 and 1024 sites respectively; earlier references to a 256-site treatment denominator apply only to L=16. The treatment-minus-control difference is -0.11705780029296875, with exploratory 95% paired Student t interval [-0.16213546788533062, -0.07198013270060688] from eight independent paired endpoints, each averaging 16 configurations. This interval lies below -0.05, meeting the numerical comparison criterion within its exploratory scope. Round 1's interval crossed -0.05; this wider size contrast now supports prioritizing independent confirmation over further size escalation. Sanity passed, consistent with the empty L=8 graph's expected fraction 1/64; replay passed, supporting repeatability. Source seed, page 2: "Isolated sites are components of size 1." Neither pass establishes general SCC or lattice correctness. Stop because no rounds remain; the result supports a finite-size decrease, not quantitative exponent agreement or the untested reversal hypothesis.
next_decision.result_interpretation: The L=32 mean largest SCC fraction was lower than the L=8 mean by more than 0.05 throughout the exploratory paired interval.
